newsitem.title: CHINA: China urges world not to fall for Taiwan plots.
newsitem.headline: China urges world not to fall for Taiwan plots.

text.p: China urged countries to be on guard against plots to win their recognition by its rival Taiwan and warned on Friday of damage to their ties with Beijing after Fiji signed a mutual-recognition communique with Taiwan.

"The Taiwan province is an inalienable part of China and... we are firmly opposed to countries which have diplomatic relations with China having official relations or carrying out official contacts with Taiwan," a Foreign Ministry official said.

The Pacific island nation Fiji, a diplomatic ally of China, signed a mutual-recognition communique with Taiwan on Friday, risking friction with the Nationalist-ruled island's powerful communist rival.

Taiwan's exiled Republic of China government has diplomatic ties with only 30 states, mainly in Africa and central America. The rest of the world recognises Beijing's communist government as the only legitimate Chinese sovereign.
All countries should recognise China in line with United Nations resolutions, the Foreign Ministry official said.
"We urge these countries to be on guard against the political plots by the Taiwan authorities so as to prevent any damage to the relations between the two countries," he said.
He declined to say whether China would break off relations with Fiji.
Beijing has regarded Taiwan as a renegade province since a civil war split them in 1949 and refuses to recognise any country that has official ties with the island.
In Taipei, Foreign Minister John Chang said the status of ties following the communique was just below establishment of diplomatic relations.
